Definition: from G1056; Galilean or belonging to Galilea:--Galilean, of Galilee.
BiblicalUsage: Galilean means a man of Galilee, and it was a word that marked a man out. A damsel said to Peter in Matthew 26:69, Thou also wast with Jesus of Galilee, and on the day of Pentecost the crowd marvelled, saying, Are not all these which speak Galilaeans, in Acts 2:7. The accent and the home gave them away.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe being a Galilean was both a shame and a glory; men despised the region, yet Jesus chose Galileans for His apostles, and I hold that God still chooses the unregarded to carry His word.
